title: He Survived 438 Days Lost at Sea #shorts

lines.text: In 2012, a fisherman was blown out to sea, and he drifted across the Pacific for more than a year.
He had no way home, so he caught fish and birds with his bare hands, and drank rainwater and turtle blood.
After 438 days, his boat washed up in the Marshall Islands, thousands of miles away.
Many doubted him, but scientists say ocean currents could carry a boat there. So, could you survive a year at sea?

sources: https://allthatsinteresting.com/jose-alvarenga (left Costa Azul Mexico Nov 17 2012 in a skiff, storm; about 438 days adrift, about 6,000 miles, to the Marshall Islands; rainwater, caught fish, turtles, seabirds by hand, turtle blood when no rain; University of Hawaii study found currents could carry the skiff there)

https://www.nationalgeographic.com/science/article/140205-science-castaway-adrift-shipwreck-survival (13 months, about 6,700 miles / 10,800 km per his account; some skepticism from Marshall Islands police; CNN weather producer found timing plausible)

facts.hedge: 438 days is his account; script says 'after 438 days' and 'many doubted him'; omits the disputed lawsuit and companion's death
